headline: A full design-system Tabs is where a dynamic prop closure blocks folding: `styled(TabInternal)` keeps its runtime call, and next-yak's styled lane runs at half its own css-prop sibling.

microbench.why: The tab group carries a state matrix, responsive typography and an animated underline through CSS anchor positioning, and the active state arrives as a prop. `next-yak-css` at 161,000 renders/s and `vanilla` at 158,000 lead, both emitting plain elements with one class each. The styled lane cannot follow: `Tab` compiles to `styled(TabInternal)("yWZDb8a7", ({ isActive }) => …)`, and a dynamic interpolation over a custom component leaves the runtime call in place, so `next-yak` lands at 80,800 and only 1.11× above its own `foldStatic: false` lane. Lanes that name classes after their declarations pay in React instead of in the library: `bamboo` books 0.034 ms of lib self-time and still totals 2.95 ms, 2.67 ms of it React writing long class attributes. `emotion` at 22,800 re-hashes the state matrix for every tab.

autocannon.why: `vanilla` at 730 req/s and `next-yak-css` at 684 lead. `next-yak` at 446 and `next-yak-nofold` at 362 finish close together, which is the render story again: with the fold blocked there is little left for it to remove. `panda-props` at 88 req/s is the floor.

attribution.why: `next-yak-css` at 1.28 ms and `vanilla` at 1.37 ms hold the floor with 0.000 ms of lib self-time. `next-yak` needs 2.24 ms with 0.847 ms of lib time, because the dynamic `isActive` interpolation keeps the runtime `styled()` call alive. Further down the cost leaves the library entirely: `bamboo` spends 2.67 ms of its 2.95 ms inside React, and `panda-props` books 6.88 ms as component self-time.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

hydrate.why: Six lanes hydrate between 45.1 ms and 47.6 ms. `goober` at 188 ms and `styled-components` at 190 ms need four times that, rebuilding a full state matrix in the client before React can attach.

inp.why: Ten lanes answer a tab switch between 7.0 ms and 8.0 ms. `styled-components` needs 11.8 ms, `goober` 13.6 ms, `panda-props` 23.7 ms and `emotion` 26.5 ms, all of them re-deriving the state matrix on the tab that changed.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: Eight lanes mount between 88.0 ms and 97.1 ms. `goober` at 188 ms, `styled-components` at 192 ms and `emotion` at 215 ms build their sheets during the mount itself.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, and its cost splits in two: 0.871 ms to 1.02 ms for twelve lanes, then 1.66 ms to 1.71 ms for `emotion`, `styled-components` and `goober`, the three that inject their sheet at render time.

payload.why: `vanilla` at 2,690 gz B and `next-yak-css` at 2,707 B set the floor, with `next-yak` adding 805 B for its runtime. The gap to the rest is the widest in the suite: `cnfast` at 22.0 kB and `tailwind-merge` at 21.1 kB carry both a merge runtime and long class lists in the markup, roughly eight times what the leading lanes ship for the same 150 tab groups.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

nsweep.why: Scaling the tab count separates static resolution from everything else. `vanilla` at 29.1 ms, `stylex` at 29.6 ms and `next-yak-css` at 31.2 ms hold a line, while `next-yak` reaches 66.3 ms because the blocked fold leaves a runtime call per tab. `panda-props` at 279 ms shows what per-instance object resolution does to a slope.

crossCase: The Example `multifile-composition` shown below is this exact workload with the styled primitives moved into an imported `parts.tsx`, and nothing meaningful moves: `next-yak` runs 80,800 here against 85,900 there, a difference inside the run-to-run spread, because that module keeps the primitives and their JSX use sites together, which is all folding requires. Contrast the Example `multifile-shop`, where primitives ship for another module's JSX to use and `next-yak` gives up 43% of its throughput.
